instruction: Order Sheet1 rows 2 through 41 by Civil Status (A-Z), then apply yellow fill to the first data row.

metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting data by Civil Status column (alphabetically: Married, Single, Widow) and highlighting row 2. After alphabetical ascending sort, the first values will be 'Married' (11 occurrences). Evaluator verifies both sorting (50% score) and highlighting of cells A2:D2 (50% score).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: (1) sorting by Civil Status column in ascending alphabetical order (40% score), and (2) highlighting entire first row of data with yellow fill (50% score)

Row integrity check is robust (getters/calc.py:66-71, metrics/calc.py:39-64): Captures reference_relationships (name->civil_status tuples) from original data and verifies these relationships are preserved after sorting by comparing sets. This ensures rows moved together during sort, not just column C sorted independently

Dynamic column detection (getters/calc.py:79-84): Uses ws.max_column to determine actual number of columns and checks all columns in row 2 for highlighting, correctly handling 'entire first row of data' requirement regardless of actual column count
Yellow color detection logic is correct (getters/calc.py:86-110): Properly identifies yellow fill colors using RGB threshold check (R>200, G>200, B<100) and handles both RGB and ARGB formats
Expected parameter handling is correct: Metric function directly accesses expected.get('sort_order'), which is correct for type='rule' since framework passes config['rules'] directly
Postconfig is appropriate: Activates window and saves file with Ctrl+S to ensure file state is fresh for verification
Partial credit scoring is reasonable: 40% for sorting correctness, 10% for row integrity, 50% for highlighting coverage
